business_problem: Semir wanted to embed text-to-image AIGC deeply into fashion design and broader apparel workflows, but building a GPU cluster from scratch would have required large capital decisions, long procurement cycles, and ongoing isolation or scheduling work. The company needed an easier way to test and scale generative design without overcommitting to fixed infrastructure.
solution_summary: Semir adopted Alibaba Cloud Function Compute as the serverless base for its AIGC design workflow and used Stable Diffusion as the image- generation engine. Function Compute provides virtualized GPU resources that can be scaled per request instead of through long-lived cluster planning, and it supports multiple card types plus very small 1 GB GPU slices so design workloads can start cheaply and scale only when needed. Around the model itself, Semir built AI inference applications and serving logic on top of the serverless runtime so designers could submit prompts, switch models without heavy tenant interference, and avoid the long queues common in shared local WebUI setups. Because the platform includes monitoring, logging, and alarm capabilities by default, the company could focus on testing how AIGC fits apparel design instead of first building a complex ops stack. The result was a practical, low-friction path from experimentation to production design support.

solution_components.name: Function Compute
solution_components.role: Provides the serverless GPU runtime and scaling layer for Semir's AIGC design applications.

solution_components.name: Stable Diffusion
solution_components.role: Generates apparel design images from prompts as the core AIGC model engine.

solution_components.name: GPU resource pool
solution_components.role: Supplies elastic virtualized GPU capacity, including small-slice configurations for cost-efficient inference.

data_flow: Designers submit prompts into the Function Compute-based inference application, where Stable Diffusion loads on elastic GPU resources, generates candidate design drafts, and returns them to the apparel workflow. Monitoring and scaling are handled by the serverless platform so peak creative demand can be absorbed without a dedicated cluster-operations team.
business_outcome: Semir moved AIGC apparel design from an expensive infrastructure decision into a practical production workflow. The serverless design stack can generate design drafts in 30 seconds, avoid the three-day turnaround common in earlier manual cycles, and keep GPU utilization above 70%, giving the company a faster and less risky path to applying AI across product design and related creative work.
